title: Rents and living costs in the 1930s
summary: Her aunt's five-room house cost $18 a month and her own one-bedroom flat $16.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: I remember the first apartment, when I first came here, as I told you before, I lived with my aunt, and my aunt had a five room house, a very nice five room house, on the
east side, one block from Central Avenue. She was paying, I think, $18.00 a month for that. A five room house with a nice lawn, a big house.

Then later, when I got my own apartment, or my mother's sister and I got an apartment together, her older sister, and my aunt -- that sister didn't stay here. She was going to move down to Los Angeles from Oakland, and she just didn't like here, so she left, and of course the apartment was mine, see. And I think I was paying $16.00 a month for this little one bedroom apartment.

So at that time, as I say, money -- nobody was making money, but everything was, you know, in accord with what you earned, because you could at that time take maybe -- you could take as little as $5.00 and live a week off that. Less than that, no doubt, you know.
